# Exact two-cap obstruction under integer-fiber width normalization

This is an upper-bound obstruction for a fixed cap count and budget.
It does not rule out upper bounds specifically at the full mixed Helly
cap count, and it is not an OC counterexample.

For z=(z_1,...,z_4) in {0,1}^4 put

 k(z)=z_1+2z_2+4z_3+8z_4,
 h_z=256^(k(z)).

For L>=1 define the actual five-dimensional convex body

 C_L=conv union_(z in {0,1}^4) ({z} x [L h_z,L h_z+1]).

Its exact integer fibers are the sixteen prescribed unit intervals:
each binary base point is an extreme point of the projection cube, so
no other fiber can contribute to its convex combinations. The body is
full-dimensional, and its mixed mass is M=16. The integer-fiber
difference body is

 D_int=conv union_z (K_z-K_z)=[-1,1].

Thus the normalization h_(D_int)(u)=1 is exactly u=+1 or u=-1.

For N=2 and cap budget tau=1/2, full closed covers exist. Take the two
opposite horizontal caps separated at any threshold strictly between
L h_7+1 and L h_8. Each contains exactly eight whole fibers, has mass
tau M=8, and their union contains S. The continuously normalized
hinge compactness theorem therefore gives an attained minimum.

Nevertheless EVERY full cover by two caps with this width normalization,
even without imposing their mass budgets, satisfies

 Psi>=L/120.                                             (1)

All parameters n=4,d=1,N=2,tau=1/2 and the width body D_int are fixed,
while the normalized hinge minimum diverges.

## 1. A rational no-six-affine-graph certificate

For any six distinct binary vertices, the six vectors (1,z) in R^5
are dependent. Choose a minimal dependent subset, of size at most six.
Signed minors of a full-rank row submatrix give a nonzero integer
dependence c_z satisfying

 sum c_z=0,   sum c_z z=0,   |c_z|<=5!=120.             (2)

For precision, if this subset has rank r, select r independent rows
and use the signed r-by-r minors of its r-by-(r+1) matrix. Its kernel
agrees with that of the full selected columns, because both have
dimension one. The entries are zero or one, so the determinant
expansion bounds every minor by r!<=120. Extend c by zero to the
original six vertices.

Such a nonzero dependence cannot annihilate their heights. If K is
the largest code with nonzero c, then

 |sum c_z h_z|
 >=256^K-120 sum_(k=0)^(K-1)256^k
 =256^K-120(256^K-1)/255>0.

The sum is an integer, and hence

 |sum c_z h_z|>=1.                                    (3)

In particular no six prescribed height points lie on a graph affine
in z. This argument covers dependent cube subsets as well as those
of full affine rank; no generic-position assumption is being used.

## 2. Lower bound for every two-cap cover

Write the two margins as

 L_i(z,x)=a_i.z+u_i x-b_i,   u_i in {-1,1}.

Assign each fiber center x=L h_z+1/2 to one cap which contains it.
At least one cap receives at least eight centers. Choose six of its
assigned vertices and let c_z be the dependence in (2). Its center
margins m_z=L_i(z,L h_z+1/2) are nonnegative. Affine cancellation gives

 sum c_z m_z=u_i L sum c_z h_z,

whose absolute value is at least L by (3). On an assigned unit fiber,
Jensen for the positive part gives

 integral_(Lh_z)^(Lh_z+1) [L_i(z,x)]_+ dx
       >=[L_i(z,Lh_z+1/2)]_+=m_z.

These six fiber contributions are disjoint portions of the total
hinge potential. Therefore

 L<=|sum c_z m_z|
   <=120 sum m_z
   <=120 Psi.

This proves (1), allowing arbitrary and unbounded integer coefficients
a_i and arbitrary offsets. Closed center membership is enough; there
is no discarded boundary mass.

## 3. Distinguishing integer widths from same-real-base widths

Let

 D_all=(C_L-C_L) intersect ({0}^4 x R)=[-W_L,W_L]

after identifying the vertical line with R. Unlike D_int, this body
records differences between points at the same REAL base, which need
not be integer. At base (1/2,1/2,0,0), compare the midpoint of the upper
endpoints at codes 0,3 with the midpoint of the lower endpoints at
codes 1,2. They give

 W_L>=1+(L/2)(256^3-256^2-256+1)
     =1+(L/2)255^2*257.                              (4)

Thus D_all normalization scales with L and is not contradicted by
(1). Treating D_int and D_all as the same width would lose this exact
nonaffine integer-fiber displacement.

At the full Helly cap count N_0=2^4(1+1)=32, the same family DOES have
a bounded D_int-normalized cover. Isolate each binary fiber with an
integer tilt and use its two half-interval caps through its midpoint.
Each has mass 1/2 and hinge 1/8. The full cover therefore has

 tau=1/32,   Psi=32/8=4=M/4,

independent of L. It is also feasible at the larger budget tau=1/2.
Consequently the two-cap obstruction does not falsify a proposed upper
bound specifically at the full Helly cap count.

These bodies are themselves exactly OC-sharp for n=4,d=1. At every
fiber midpoint, any closed ambient halfspace has own-fiber mass at
least 1/2. Conversely any point lies in an own-fiber half-interval of
mass at most 1/2, and its extreme binary fiber permits an integer tilt
excluding all other fibers. Hence maximal normalized depth is
1/(2M)=1/32. Under D_all normalization the thirty-two-cap construction
has Psi/M=1/(4W_L)->0 by (4), so that normalization cannot give a
uniform positive normalized hinge lower bound even on sharp families.
